svg.title: Lost-Subject Profiles: Downed Pilot vs. Civilian Hiker
svg.desc: One-slide rescue-planning comparison with matched semi-realistic editorial illustrations.
svg.text: Lost-Subject Profiles: Downed Pilot vs. Civilian Hiker
Rescue-planning baseline: either subject may be injured, displaced, and without a detectable signal.

g.text: Beacon or radio may be silent
Do not assume an active emitter
May follow trails or seek water
May stop, backtrack, or seek shelter
Phone or watch may be silent
No formal survival training; may rely on
common sense and basic outdoor skills
406 MHz PLB, aircraft ELT, satellite radio
Ejection damage, depleted battery, or injury;
or powered off to conserve battery
May leave the chute or wreckage and hide;
may move at night toward a planned pickup point
May follow trails, descend toward water or roads,
backtrack, seek shelter, or stay put
Mirror, strobe, IR marker, or brief radio
phone if powered and within coverage
Crash site and chute as starting points;
radio transmissions, thermal/IR, and hide sites
Visual, thermal, and acoustic search; trails,
water routes, phone, or Bluetooth signals
Plan for visual, thermal, acoustic, and ground search; treat any verified signal as supplemental.
Illustrations and behavioral assumptions are planning references; equipment, condition, and response are not guaranteed.
